questions: What is the exact definition of "p divides N an even number of times" - does this mean the exponent of p in the prime factorization of N is even?
Is 1 considered a valid 400 number since it has zero prime factors, which could be interpreted as having an even count of each prime factor?
How should ties be broken when there are multiple 400 numbers with the same maximum value not exceeding A?
Are the prime factors required to be distinct, or can they include repeated primes with even exponents?
What should be returned if there is no 400 number not exceeding A (though given the constraint A ≥ 36, this may be impossible)?
Does the term "exactly 2 distinct prime factors" mean exactly two different primes, or exactly two prime factors counting multiplicity?
Should the output format include any specific spacing or newline requirements between query results?
Are there any additional implicit constraints on the input values that aren't explicitly stated in the constraints section?

A positive integer N is a 400 number if and only if it satisfies both of the following two conditions:
- N has exactly 2 distinct prime factors.
- For each prime factor p of N, the maximum integer k such that p^k divides N is even. In other words, all exponents in the prime factorization of N are even. 
Process Q queries. Each query gives you an integer A, so find the largest 400 number not exceeding A. 
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
Q
\text{query}_1
\text{query}_2
\vdots
\text{query}_Q
Here, \text{query}_i is the i-th query, given in the following format:
A
Output
Print the result. 
Constraints
- 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5
- For each query, 36 \leq A \leq 10^{12}.
- All input values are integers.
